text:
Andrea Park: Quick sync — product wants a per-org customer dashboard that shows cost, p95 latency, KV cache health, and a noisy-neighbor score. Need inputs from runtime + infra on metric availability and the ingest API we should use.

Samir Khan: Do we already emit per-org labels everywhere? we have org_id on request logs but not on all runtime metrics. tagging will be the main lift.

Megan Li: Right — serving runtime currently emits shard-level metrics with optional org tag via the envoy sidecar. Adding org tag to token-level counters will cost CPU/allocs. We can add a sampled-org mode for top customers.

Tony Reyes: From console UX: customers expect a single toggle in the Console to opt-into per-org dashboards (privacy/legal). Also need role-based access so org admins see their org only.

Shreya Patel: SRE concern: per-org cardinality explosion. We should compute aggregated signals at ingest (e.g., per-org p95 from histogram buckets) and only forward derived metrics to long-term store.

Andrea Park: Good point. We want 3-day retention for the UI and 90-day for billing. Can we sketch minimal derived metrics?

Samir Khan: Minimal set (exports):
```
- redwood.requests_per_min{org_id}
- redwood.tokens_generated_per_min{org_id}
- redwood.latency_p95_org{org_id}
- redwood.kv_cache_hit_rate{org_id}
- redwood.noisy_neighbor_index{org_id}
```
We can compute latency_p95_org from latency_histogram by doing aggregations at the push gateway.

Megan Li: noisy_neighbor_index needs combining signals: sudden drop in kv_cache_hit_rate, spike in tail latency, worker_cpu_steal, and queue_backlog. We'll implement a sliding-window score at ingest: 0..100.

Tony Reyes: UX asks that noisy_neighbor_index be bucketed into: Normal / Elevated / Critical and provide a short explanation tooltip. Also button to open tenant isolation playbook.

Andrea Park: API contract debate: console wants a single "per-org-insights" endpoint that returns metrics + annotations. infra prefers separate metrics store + metadata API. Thoughts?

Samir Khan: Separate APIs is cleaner: metrics via Prometheus (or metrics store) and metadata (org config, quota tier) via internal REST. Console can join them. Single endpoint hides where data comes from.

Megan Li: If we do separate, add a stable contract for the ingest-derived metrics. Suggest versioned metric names and a feature-flagged rollout.

Shreya Patel: Proposal for noisy neighbor detection rollout:
- Phase 1: Sampled per-org metrics for top 100 orgs (2 weeks)
- Phase 2: Aggregated derived metrics for all orgs (compute at ingest) behind FF (4 weeks)
- Phase 3: UI rollout canary to 10% customers + ops alerting (2 weeks)

Andrea Park: That timeline is acceptable. Who owns the ingest compute job?

Megan Li: Infra owns the aggregator; runtime will add org tagging and sampling. SRE owns alerting and thresholds. Console team owns the UI and access controls.

Tony Reyes: UX notes: need mock JSON payload for the endpoint so we can build the panel without live data. example payload please.

Samir Khan: Mock payload (suggested):
```
{
  "org_id": "org_123",
  "period": "2026-04-01T00:00:00Z/2026-04-01T01:00:00Z",
  "metrics": {
    "requests_per_min": 420,
    "tokens_per_min": 32000,
    "latency_p95_ms": 210,
    "kv_cache_hit_rate": 0.87,
    "noisy_neighbor_index": 12
  },
  "annotations": ["cache_warmup", "behind_quota" ]
}
```

Tony Reyes: Perfect. We'll start building the panel with that.

Shreya Patel: Alerting: create an SLO for per-org p95 > 500ms and noisy_neighbor_index > 60 triggers paging. For elevated (30-60) send Ops Slack warning only.

Andrea Park: Two policy questions: 1) Do we allow customer-level ad-hoc queries on raw event logs? 2) How do we avoid PII exposure in per-org metrics?

Megan Li: 1) No direct raw dumps; provide aggregated query endpoints. 2) Strip user identifiers at source; org_id is fine. Keep request text out of metrics.

Samir Khan: Also debating: routing fallback when noisy neighbor detected. Runtime can temporarily route to isolated capacity or degrade to cheaper model. Need a routing policy API:
```
POST /internal/routing/policy
payload: { org_id, condition: "noisy_neighbor_index>60", action: "route:isolation-v2" }
```

Andrea Park: We should treat routing changes as reversible automated actions with audit logs. Ops wants ability to override.

OpsBot: Reminder: RFC for per-org routing policies is in #eng-runtime, link: https://rwd.internal/rfc/279

Samir Khan: Implementors note: routing decisions need to be low-latency. We'll push decisions to a distributed config cache rather than call the central API per request.

Megan Li: Data retention note: store derived per-org metrics in metrics-db with org_id partitioning to make queries efficient.

Andrea Park: Action items:
- Samir: prototype tagging + mock payload by EOW (2060012400)
- Megan: design ingest aggregator + noise index formula draft (2060012440)
- Tony: console mockups + RBAC flow (2060012460)
- Shreya: alert thresholds + runbook draft (2060012470)
- All: sync next Tue 10am PT to review canary plan

Samir Khan: ack. I'll post a short PR with sampling config and a prometheus scrape example.

Megan Li: I'll draft the ingest job and link the datastore schema.

Andrea Park: Thanks everyone. tagging @Shreya @Tony for follow-ups. :thumbsup:

DevBot: Deploy bot — sampling-config branch deployed to staging (build 4421).

OpsBot: Created incident playbook stub: /playbooks/noisy-neighbor.md

Tony Reyes: I'll add the mock JSON to the design Figma and share the link in the thread.

Andrea Park: End of thread — will post meeting notes after Tue sync.
